composing_text: 4th Special Service Brigade; elements of 79th Armoured Division
notes: Assault corps (Crocker) at Juno and Sword plus Orne airborne flank; Caen not taken on D-Day and I Corps linked with XXX Corps by end of D-Day.

current_activity: delayed 51st Highland Division attack from the Orne bridgehead, contained by 21st Panzer; bridgehead also under attack
notes: I Corps' planned eastern thrust (51st (Highland) Division and 4th Armoured Brigade crossing into the 6th Airborne Division's Orne bridgehead, toward Cagny south-east of Caen) was postponed to 12 June because bad weather delayed the landing of the 51st Division and 4th Armoured Brigade (Wikipedia, Operation Perch, citing Ellis). The corps' own attack on 12 June was limited: the bridgehead was itself attacked all day from the Bréville area (346th Infantry Division per the Battle of Bréville page; the 21st Panzer Division was also opposing from the south), the Germans pulled back in the evening, and 12th Parachute Battalion and a Devonshire company captured Bréville that night. The 51st Division, opposed by 21st Panzer in its push south toward Sainte-Honorine, was contained, and the offensive east of Caen was called off on 13 June. The fighting was done by divisions (51st Highland, 6th Airborne), not by the corps headquarters; the point is a representative bridgehead point (Bréville-les-Monts commune coordinates), not the corps HQ. current_activity: pinning 21st Panzer east of the Orne before Epsom
notes: 51st Division (152nd Bde) attacked 23 June toward Sainte-Honorine-la-Chardronette east of the Orne to pin 21st Panzer before Epsom. Exact village not geocoded; position is the Orne bridgehead.

current_activity: Charnwood: I Corps attacks to clear Caen as far as the Orne; by 18:00 on 9 July it reaches the river at Caen
notes: Event date: 8 July 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, pp. 310, 311, 312, 316, 317). Event definition: I Corps, reinforced to about 115,000 men, attacks on 8 July (the full artillery programme opened at 04:20, p. 313) to clear Caen as far as the Orne and to seize bridgeheads south of the city; on 9 July it reaches the Orne at Caen by 18:00 and the Odon above its junction with the Orne (p. 316). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, pp. 310-312: "On that day I Corps, strongly reinforced and now comprising about 115,000 officers and men, was to clear Caen as far as the river Orne and establish bridgeheads across the river south of the city"; pp. 316-317: "by 6 p.m. I Corps had reached the Orne at Caen". Location: Caen, Calvados (existing place PL0057) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is Caen city, the objective; the corps headquarters is not named on the pages. Location support: Ellis names Caen as the objective of the corps and the Orne at Caen as the line reached (pp. 310 and 316). Commander: Lt.-Gen. J. T. Crocker (Ellis, vol. I, p. 170 names him as the I Corps commander at the landings and p. 432 as the corps commander in August).

current_activity: Goodwood: I Corps is to hold the east flank area Bures-Troarn-St. Pair-Emieville-Touffreville with the 3rd Division
notes: Event date: 18 July 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, p. 336). Event definition: I Corps' task in Goodwood is to establish the 3rd British Infantry Division in the east flank area of Bures, Troarn, St. Pair, Emieville and Touffreville and to hold it against attack from the east and south-east, while VIII Corps strikes south on its right (p. 336); the division starts at 07:45 (p. 343). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 336: "I Corps was to establish the 3rd British Infantry Division in the east flank area of Bures-Troarn-St. Pair-Emiéville—Touffreville and to hold it against attack from the east and south-east". Location: Troarn, Calvados (new place) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is Troarn, the middle village of the east flank area named in the order; the corps headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names the area and Troarn as its centre of gravity (p. 336). Commander: Lt.-Gen. J. T. Crocker (Ellis, vol. I, p. 170 names him as the I Corps commander at the landings and p. 432 as the corps commander in August).

current_activity: Passes from Second Army to First Canadian Army at noon; Stacey calls it 1st British Corps
notes: Event date: 23 July 1944, noon (Stacey, p. 196). Event definition: The corps front east of the Orne passes from Second Army to the headquarters of First Canadian Army, which becomes operational at noon; the corps stays under the Army until March 1945 (p. 198). This is the only claim of I Corps in Canadian Batch 1: a minimal record kept as evidence for the command relations, not a unit claim set (the British batch comes later). Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 196: "at noon on 23 July Headquarters First Canadian Army became operational, though as yet it had no Canadian divisions under its command. It took over at that moment the front held by Lieut.-General J. T. Crocker's 1st British Corps"; p. 198: "the 1st British Corps operated under the First Canadian Army through the weeks and months that followed". Location: Orne bridgehead / east of Caen (existing area place PL0265) with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point is the existing area place east of Caen and stands for the corps front; it is not a headquarters position. Location support: Stacey (p. 196) gives the corps front only as the area between the Caen-Mezidon railway and the Channel, with no town. Commander: Lt.-Gen. J. T. Crocker.
